LESSON: READING 15.4.1 POEMS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 15
Topic 15.4: Reading 15.4.1 Poems
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 15.4.1 Poems, part of Strand 15 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: Which lessons have you learnt from poems before? 2. How can you say what is in the poem in your own words?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 15.4.1 Poems together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Problem solving is enhanced as learners get ideas from poems on how to solve problems of self and others.

• Self-efficacy is enhanced as the learner focuses on achieving set tasks while reciting and dramatising poems.

Values:
Respect is enriched as the learners provide feedback on lessons identified by peers with dignity.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Social cohesion is nurtured as learners appreciate the role of their peers as they recite and dramatise the poems.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:


Remember the key question: Which lessons have you learnt from poems before? 2. How can you say what is in the poem in your own words?
